name: tractor_front
source: Plausible Magic Formula coefficients for a radial agricultural front tyre (e.g. 480/65R24 class), following Pacejka 'Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics' 3rd ed. ch. 4's MF5.2 structure. Peak friction on a firm/paved surface (Dx1/Dy1 ~= 0.85) and higher rolling resistance/lower stiffness than a passenger radial reflect the general agricultural-tyre trends reported in Wong, 'Theory of Ground Vehicles', 5th ed., ch. 1 (Table 1.3) and ch. 2 - not a measured/proprietary .tir. unloaded_radius=0.8 m matches data/models/tractor/tractor.rig.json's front wheel radius. PHYS-036 (2026-09-24): same 'aligning' sign/shape fix as data/tyres/passenger_car_225_45r17.json - qdz1/qdz2 flipped (was +0.11/-0.02) so Mz0 = -t*Fy0 (Pacejka's own convention, Dz opposite sign to Dy) instead of reinforcing Fy0; qbz1 raised from 6.0 to 52.8 (same B-scaling technique, shape unchanged) so the curve peaks at ~4.5 deg of slip (a larger, softer ag tyre's trail is expected to fall off a little later than a stiffer passenger tyre's ~4 deg, still well inside the qualitative 2-6 deg range Milliken ch. 2 and Wong ch. 2 describe) instead of the un-fixed curve's ~39.6 deg. Longitudinal shape refit (2026-09-25, alongside data/tyres/passenger_car_225_45r17.json's): pcx1 1.6 -> 1.42 and pex1 0.05 -> -0.55; pdx*/pkx* unchanged. The old C put the Fx0 large-slip asymptote at sin(C*pi/2) = 0.59 of peak (Fx(kappa=1)/peak 0.71, Fx(kappa=3)/peak 0.63), inconsistent with this file's own lateral block (pcy1 1.3, asymptote 0.89) and with agricultural drive tyres' measured traction-vs-slip curves, which on firm ground fall only mildly past the peak and on soil keep rising toward 100% slip (Wong ch. 2/Brixius-type net-traction curves) - an ag tyre that loses 40% of its drive once it slips is the wrong direction. Same target band as the passenger tyre (Fx(kappa=1)/peak ~0.84, Fx(kappa=3)/peak ~0.81); E=-0.55 rather than -0.45 keeps peak slip at 0.143 at fz0, no later than before (an ag tyre's peak slip is expected at or a little above a passenger tyre's, so not pulled lower). Rolling resistance (2026-10-06, tyre crr work): qsy1/qsy3/qsy4 are now DERIVED from the rolling_resistance anchor block - crr = crr_base*(1 + A*(v/V_r) + B*(v/V_r)^4) with crr(0.8 V_r) = 1.5 crr_base and crr(V_r) = 2.0 crr_base [AS: the 1.5/2.0 rise anchors sit between the Gillespie and Wong passenger-tyre forms, neither re-checked against a readable source], rated speed V_r [C] ETRTO agricultural speed symbol D = 65 km/h (from memory, not re-read) - above the tractor_12f4r top speed of 2650 rpm limiter / 12th gear = 47.8 km/h; replaces the raw qsy4 0.0002*(v/16.7)^4 (tractor 0.0003*(v/8.3)^4) which cost 30x the base at 370 km/h on the hypercar.
